milestone_successes: FoVer corpus expanded to 6548 pairs (13x above 500-pair target): GGUF pre-download fix from .82 design finally resolved the MetaQA silent-stub pattern that had persisted across .80 and .81. Z3 confirmed 6332 new pairs from GSM8K dataset.

Probe ensemble AUROC breakthrough: best_probe_auroc=0.9899 (sos_kan), up from 0.5694 in .81. This is a direct consequence of the corpus expansion — 30x more training data transformed three below-threshold probes into near-perfect classifiers (ThinkPRM 0.9885, NK-KAEM 0.9875). GS-KAN INT8 quantization (0.5063) remains below threshold but GS-KAN float (0.2638) is a known architectural limitation.

WOPR Sudoku code complete with all specs satisfied locally: 4 easter eggs pass, Ising solver reaches E=0 in 5130 iterations, CRT aesthetic implemented. The only gap is a missing HF_TOKEN for deployment — the code itself is production-ready and can be deployed with a single environment variable.
biggest_gaps_83: EnvPropagationGuard self-heal failure is now the primary pre-test blocker. The .82 pattern differed from .81: instead of 4 failing tests, the self-heal hook itself crashed ('EnvPropagationGuard failed to load CARNOT_ variables'). Until this is fixed, any experiment that relies on pre-test surgery will recur in SKIP/FAIL. Must be diagnosed and fixed as the mandatory-first task in .83, before any other infrastructure work.

Codex agent config.toml reserved-key error blocked both WOPR cartridges (1060, 1061) with 'model_providers contains reserved' across 6 total attempts. This is a conductor-level routing bug: the codex agent_type requires a distinct Claude Code config that avoids conflicting with reserved model_providers keys. Must be fixed before WOPR cartridges can run. WOPR gallery is now 3 milestones behind known-issues.md mandate.

Gate coercion (exp1052) and DualGPU torch install (exp1053) remain undeployed for the 5th+ consecutive milestone, cascading to block Triple Integration (4th consecutive GATE_BLOCK) and Zenil alpha_t FR-11 (3rd consecutive block). These are the same root-cause chain: pre-test failures prevent the gate coercion fix; without gate coercion, DualGPU is unreachable; without DualGPU, Zenil alpha_t is blocked. EnvPropagationGuard fix (.83 mandatory-first) must land before this chain can be broken.
process_observations: Pre-test surgery deadlock recurred with new failure mode: .82 design correctly placed exp1050 as unconditional first task, but the self-heal mechanism's EnvPropagationGuard dependency introduced a new crash path. The fix cannot be bootstrapped when the framework it depends on (EnvPropagationGuard) is itself broken. .83 must treat EnvPropagationGuard repair as a meta-prerequisite that runs before pre-test surgery, not after.

Gate mechanism worked correctly as a circuit-breaker: when exp1050 produced no artifact, gate checks on exp1051 and exp1053 detected the missing upstream immediately and generated explicit blocked artifacts rather than hanging. This prevented silent loss. The gate design from .82 proposal is validated — the blocking was expected and the artifacts are correct.

Independent tracks proved resilient: exp1055 (FoVer) and exp1057 (probe ensemble) had no gate dependencies on exp1050 and both succeeded. The .82 architecture of separating hardware/infrastructure gates from corpus/probe tracks was correct in design. When infrastructure fails, research tracks that don't depend on it should continue — and they did.

Codex agent routing is a new class of failure not addressed in .82 design. The model_providers config.toml conflict was not anticipated in the parallel conductor design (exp1051). Even if exp1051 had run successfully, the Codex agent config error would have blocked exp1060/1061 anyway. .83 must include a Codex agent smoke-test as part of the parallel conductor validation.

Corpus-to-accuracy lever is now confirmed empirically: expanding training pairs from 216 to 6548 moved best probe AUROC from 0.5694 to 0.9899. This is a 74-percentile-point improvement from a 30x data increase. The FoVer corpus expansion is load-bearing for the entire probe ensemble track. Maintaining corpus quality (Z3-confirmed labels, not just synthetic) is critical for future AUROC claims.

WOPR Sudoku deployment gap (HF_TOKEN absent) is an ops-credential issue, not a code issue. The experiment design should have included a fallback that explicitly checks for the token at task-start and either injects it from SOPS or blocks with a clear 'token_required' verdict. The 'code_complete_deploy_pending' verdict is honest but the missing token should have been surfaced earlier in the task spec.
